original_question: Can the tuning construction for polynomials be carried out by quasiconformal surgery?
target_in_paper: §2. Quasiconformal Surgery, Question 5: "Can tunings be constructed with quasiconformal surgery?" This appears in the tuning subsection immediately after the paper defines the topological tuning construction and distinguishes it from neighboring questions about existence and continuity. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right operation (tuning), the right objects (polynomials), and the right method (quasiconformal surgery). It is very close to the paper's actual Question 5 and does not drift into the neighboring questions on whether tuning gives a polynomial at all or whether tuning depends continuously on parameters. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is working in one-variable complex dynamics: complex polynomials and their Julia sets, with the surgery viewed on the Riemann sphere. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The tuning setup is not for arbitrary polynomials: first choose a polynomial P1 with a periodic critical point ω of period k, and assume that no other critical points lie in the entire basin of the associated superattracting cycle. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The second polynomial P2 is assumed to have exactly one critical point, and the degree of that critical point must match the degree/local degree of ω. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
The paper also assumes that the Julia sets of both P1 and P2 are connected. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

In the first explicit description of tuning, the closure of the immediate basin of ω is assumed to be homeomorphic to the closed unit disk, and J(P2) is assumed locally connected. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The construction being asked about is the specific topological tuning just described: replace the basin of ω (and its preimages) by copies of the dynamical plane of P2, matching external angles of P2 with internal angles of the basin. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The intended outcome is not merely a topological object, but a quasiconformal realization of the tuning that yields a map conjugate to a polynomial, of the same degree as P1. Question 5 presupposes this tuning setup and asks specifically for a quasiconformal-surgery realization, whereas Question 4 separately asks whether the tuning is conjugate to a polynomial at all. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
refined_question: Let P1 be a complex polynomial with a periodic critical point ω of period k, such that no other critical points lie in the full basin of the corresponding superattracting cycle, and let P2 be a complex polynomial with exactly one critical point whose local degree equals the local degree of ω; assume that J(P1) and J(P2) are connected. In the topological tuning construction described in §2—where one replaces the immediate basin of ω and its preimages in the dynamical plane of P1 by copies of the dynamical plane of P2, matching external angles of P2 to internal angles of the basin (in the first description assuming additionally that the basin closure is a closed disk and J(P2) is locally connected)—can this tuning be realized by quasiconformal surgery? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
justification: The draft matches the paper's Question 5 almost verbatim. The surrounding context shows that the paper is not asking the broader question of whether tuning exists topologically, nor the neighboring Question 4 about whether the topological tuning is conjugate to a polynomial, nor Questions 6–8 about continuity. The sharp paper-faithful restatement therefore has to keep the precise tuning setup that immediately precedes Question 5 and then ask only whether that construction can be carried out by quasiconformal surgery. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
